upload_instructions: Set the MIDI Inter-packet delay to 30 ms.
Hold FUNCTION during power-on and select TRIG 4 (OS Upgrade).
Click 'Upload MIDI Upgrade File' below and pick the .syx file.

bank_select_reset.description: Sent alongside Panic to reset bank selects.

system.note: Each drum track answers on its own MIDI channel and owns the full CC range there, so a track needs no CC offset. The FX track and the auto-channel that addresses the selected track are both set in the MIDI CHANNELS menu, and neither number appears in the MIDI appendix, which also lists no pitch bend, so none is forwarded.

sysex_api.description: `F0 [sysex_header] [device_id] [type] [proto_version] [object_number] [footer] F7`, fifteen bytes in all. The same request frame the Analog Four uses with the product byte changed, so no existing C7 SysEx path can address the Rytm yet.
sysex_api.note: Checksums are the sum-of-bytes scheme the Analog Four introduced rather than the XOR the Machinedrum and Monomachine use. Sample transfers are the exception that works today, and they ride the Sample Dump Standard rather than this frame.

sound.note: Request workbuffers 0-11 ("SOUNDX") to retrieve the 12 track sounds of the currently loaded kit.

sample.note: A transfer lands as a file in a +Drive directory rather than a numbered slot, so the slot number only names the file.

slot.note: Object number >=128 addresses the RAM/workbuffer copy instead of a saved slot, which also switches the dump/request id to its +6 'X' variant. See `sysex_api.kit`.

unknown_1.note: Reads `00 00 00 06` on FW1.70. Possibly a format/version marker.

levels.note: 12 drum tracks plus FX track. LSB is unused, always 0.

tracks.note: One full Sound structure per drum track (FX track is not included here). Same layout as `sysex_layout.sound.fields.payload_structure`.

unknown_5.note: Observed all-zero in one captured kit, but not confirmed always zero.

unknown_7.note: [SPECULATION] Possibly the current scene id's MSB.

ctrl_in_mod_1_target_1.note: Same destination ids as sound mod targets, but the LFO-parameter destinations cannot be used here.

slot.note: Object number >=128 addresses the RAM/workbuffer copy instead of a saved slot, which also switches the dump/request id to its +6 'X' variant. See `sysex_api.sound`.

header_marker.note: Reads `BE EF BA CE 00 00 00 04 00 00 00 00` on FW1.70. Purpose unconfirmed.

synth_param_1.note: Meaning is machine-dependent, see the top-level machines section. LSB unused pre-FW1.70.

default_note.note: `$3C`=0, not used inside a standalone sound dump (only meaningful inside a kit).

slot.note: Object number >=128 addresses the RAM/workbuffer copy instead of a saved slot, which also switches the dump/request id to its +6 'X' variant. See `sysex_api.pattern`.

tracks.note: Tracks 0-11 are the 12 drum tracks, track 12 is the FX track.

trig_bits.note: 14 flag bits per step across 64 steps (896 bits / 112 bytes), not byte-aligned per step. Bits: 0=enable trig, 1=retrig, 2=mute, 3=accent, 4=swing, 5=slide, 6=enable LFO p-lock, 7=p-locked SYN state, 8=p-locked SMP state, 9=p-locked ENV state, 10=p-locked LFO state, 11=enable SYN p-lock, 12=enable SMP p-lock, 13=enable ENV p-lock.

step_notes.note: `$FF`=unset (use default note). Bit 7 clear means the step also carries a trig condition. Low 7 bits are the MIDI note.

step_note_lengths.note: `$FF`=unset (use default length). 127=infinite. The values in between follow a non-linear scale.

data.note: One value per step. The value's meaning depends on `type`.

kit_number.note: `$FF` when no kit is saved with the pattern.

bpm_msb.note: Multiplied by 120. Used when BPM mode=PTN.

pad_scale_per_pattern.fullname: Pad Scale Applies To All Tracks

slot.note: Always 0, since there is only one settings object.

bpm_msb.note: Multiplied by 120. Used when BPM mode=PRJ.

selected_track_duplicate.note: Duplicate of `selected_track`, for an unknown purpose.

selected_mode.note: Stops at 2 rather than an expected 3, possibly a firmware bug.

sample_info_table.note: [SPECULATION] Per-slot sample info/checksum block. First 4 bytes = `$FFFFFFFF` when the slot is unused. Fields within each 16-byte entry are not decoded.

slot.note: Global slot 0-3. Object number >=128 addresses the RAM/workbuffer copy, which also switches the dump/request id to its +6 'X' variant. See `sysex_api.global`.

click_pre_roll.note: 0=off, otherwise shown as 1-16 bars on the device.

unknown_4.note: Always reads zero. Exactly 16 bytes, possibly related to the 12 track channels plus a few more, unconfirmed.

note_mapping.note: The single map the device reads incoming notes with. An entry marked `per_track` walks the twelve tracks upward from the note it lists.

standard.note: The low octave fires one track each and everything above it plays the selected track chromatically.

standalone.name: Machine
standalone.note: Picks which machine the track runs, which in turn decides what the eight SYNTH parameters mean. The value that selects each machine is not in the MIDI appendix.

synth.name: SYNTH
synth.note: What each of the eight means changes with the track's machine. The machines block lists the per-machine names, and their order there is the machine's own, which is sometimes not the order the SRC page shows.

fx.name: FX
fx.note: A second CC map the FX track answers with. These numbers overlap the drum-track map in `pages.synth`, and the channel a message arrives on decides which applies. The FX channel is set in the MIDI CHANNELS menu and is not in the MIDI appendix. NRPN bank 2 is unique to this map, so NRPN addresses it without the collision.

pages.name: REVERB
pages.note: NRPN 2:14 is absent from the MIDI appendix, so the seven below are the whole page.

pages.name: DIST
pages.note: The appendix files Delay Overdrive and the two routing switches here rather than with the delay. NRPN 2:19 through 2:21 are absent from it.

machines.note: What the eight SYNTH parameters mean on a track, one entry per machine. Slots a machine does not use are left empty. The MIDI appendix gives no id for any of these, so the value CC 15 wants to select one is unknown, and it spells the slot names out rather than printing the four-character labels the screen shows.
